classes.name: ISS33-CLEANUP-FAILURE-HONESTY
classes.owner: Recorder failure/transaction boundary (`src/recorder/run.ts`, its existing public failure owner/schema, synchronized generated Recorder artifacts, and focused failure tests)
classes.boundary: A staging-tree cleanup failure occurring while Recorder is already reporting a primary Recorder/child outcome
classes.disposition: Sustained. Current-head `CLAUDE.md` requires caught causes to leave a trace absent a documented continuation contract; independent README/docs/schema/source/Issue-33 searches found no such staging-cleanup exception. The failure is reproducible without a production hook: an owned stage below an owned but mode-0500 parent makes the exact `rmSync(stage,{recursive:true,force:true})` operation throw `EACCES`, which the current empty catch discards. The transaction/failure seam owns both staging disposal and primary Recorder/child truth. Deleting the catch or rethrowing masks the primary outcome; replacing the primary diagnostic also masks it; deleting cleanup leaves the failed staging tree and changes the existing disposal behavior rather than fixing its honesty. Therefore retain cleanup and the primary failure, publish no docket, and add only the minimum bounded typed scanner-safe secondary cleanup evidence through the existing failure owner—no raw exception text/path/credential and no second logger, retry mechanism, external store, or test-only hook. The red/green oracle must induce a real cleanup failure, distinguish primary and cleanup causes, preserve child truth and exit 125, and prove no docket publication. Synchronize only the owning runtime/schema/generated surfaces required by that representation.

classes.name: ISS33-ONE-CORE-ARRAY-ADAPTER
classes.owner: Native lifecycle extractor and its focused tests (`src/recorder/extract.ts`, `test/native-session-sealer.test.ts`, and generated `dist/recorder/extract.js`)
classes.boundary: The exported test-only `extractAcceptedReceipt(rows)` array compatibility entry point versus the single streaming `AcceptanceCollector` core
classes.disposition: Sustained as unnecessary compatibility surface, not as duplicate collector logic. A fixed-HEAD `git grep` finds the symbol only in `src/recorder/extract.ts`, generated `dist/recorder/extract.js`, and the import/calls in `test/native-session-sealer.test.ts`; README and schemas contain no public v2 contract for it, and production `runRecorder` uses `AcceptanceCollector` directly. Delete the exported wrapper and exercise `AcceptanceCollector` directly in that focused test file, then rebuild the generated counterpart. Do not add another array helper/adapter, preserve a v1 compatibility entry point, duplicate collector logic, or alter owner-approved exact full package call-ID retention.

classes.name: ISS33-SECURITY-SOURCE-READABILITY
classes.boundary: Existing cleanup, destination occupancy, child settlement, failure mapping, audit-artifact storage, promotion, and signal decisions only
classes.disposition: Partially sustained under the already-authorized readability class. Rename opaque `p`, `c`, `s`, and `e` bindings where they carry paths/config, child settlement or signal, stored audit results, or caught/primary causes in these trust paths; use role-revealing names and ordinary statement boundaries without changing behavior. Reject `dest` and `err` as findings: in their local contexts they plainly denote destination and error and provide no concrete readability counterexample. Bound this repair strictly to `src/recorder/run.ts` plus its generated counterpart; add no guard, abstraction, contract change, repository-wide rename, or test churn for this class.

details.note: All Standards findings were individually adjudicated against current HEAD.
